svg.title: x86 protection rings: the innermost level is the most privileged
svg.desc: Concentric rings built from the outside in. Ring 3 runs user applications. Rings 2 and 1 are defined by the hardware but rarely used by mainstream operating systems. Ring 0 is the kernel. Ring minus 1 is the hypervisor, ring minus 2 is SMM firmware, and ring minus 3 is the security processor, Intel CSME or AMD Secure Processor, where a firmware TPM runs. Rings below 0 are informal names. Trusted execution environments, an SGX enclave in ring 3 and an Intel TDX trust domain, add isolation rather than a higher rank. The TDX module runs in SEAM, a CPU mode beside the hypervisor's VMX root, not a new ring. A discrete TPM is a separate chip on the board, outside the CPU rings.
svg.text: x86 protection rings: the innermost level is the most privileged

Rings below 0 are informal names, not hardware ring numbers. Dashed outlines mark TEEs, which add isolation rather than rank.
